role: Kavya - QA Lead / anti-vibe-code audit (RC 115f698, clean checkout at C:/Users/Sage world/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/rc-115f698)
summary: Verdict: REJECTED for go-live in two areas, CONDITIONAL elsewhere. The commit typechecks (tsc --noEmit exit 0, 0 errors) and the 3 targeted backend suites I ran are green (TransactionalOnlyOnPublicMethodsTest 2/2, ConfirmLaunchExecutorTest 9/9, CreateCampaignExecutorTest 13/13). Code-standard hygiene is good: 0 console.log, 0 ts-ignore, and effectively no 'any' in non-test src. The real defects are in state, money and wiring. (1) The Meera brand funding flow at /brand/meera has no working live path. MeeraWorkspace.handlePay funds the hardcoded campaign id 'meera_demo_campaign', which gets a 404 from EscrowService.deriveFundAmount, and the request_payment 'Confirm payment' link points to /brand/escrow/fund, which has no SPA route and lands on NotFoundPage. (2) Seven @Transactional methods are inert, and the repo's own test allowlists them as KNOWN_INERT. Two of these are real multi-write paths with no atomicity: MeeraSessionService.doSendTurn (charges an AI credit, then persists) and CreateCampaignExecutor.doExecute (saves campaign, intent, tool-call and audit rows; a retry can create a duplicate campaign). (3) ConfirmLaunchExecutor moves a campaign to ACTIVE with none of the CampaignValidator gates that the human PATCH path enforces (workspace verification, not COMPLETED or CANCELLED, HYPE config). (4) The platform fee is resolved from at least 4 divergent sources: yml 15% (AmountDerivationService, which quotes the Meera payment), DB brand_fee_bps 10%, a PRO plan override that /brand/platform-fee ignores, and a FE hardcode of 15% in creator-chat.tsx. (5) The in-memory rate-limit map in AuthRateLimitFilter never evicts entries. Engineering quality: 13 Java services are over 800 lines (DealService 2523). 7 methods are over 150 lines (CreateCampaignExecutor.doExecute 276). 15 TSX files are over 1100 lines (creator-chat 3272, brand-chat 3003). There are 3 FE API layers (api.ts 7037 lines, meera-api.ts 905, admin api-contracts.ts 1546), and POST /wallet/escrow/fund is wrapped in two of them. Helper copies are duplicated across the Meera executors and the two chat pages. Admin endpoints return bare DTOs while 77 of the user controllers use the ApiResponse envelope.

questions.question: Can a brand actually fund and launch a campaign through the Meera workspace (/brand/meera) in live mode?
questions.why_it_matters: /brand/meera is in the brand sidebar (brand-layout.tsx:124) and the command bar, so it is a primary surface that handles money.
questions.answer: No. The Pay CTA calls MeeraWorkspace.handlePay, which POSTs /wallet/escrow/fund with campaignId 'meera_demo_campaign' (MeeraWorkspace.tsx:21,76-77). EscrowService.deriveFundAmount does findByIdAndWorkspaceId(campaignId, workspaceId).orElseThrow, so the request 404s. The request_payment tool card renders an <a href='/brand/escrow/fund?campaignIntentId=...'> (RequestPaymentExecutor.confirmActionUrl:181-183, ToolResultRenderer.tsx:283-290), and App.tsx has no /brand/escrow route (only the '*' NotFoundPage at :883).
questions.remaining_uncertainty: Not runtime-reproduced (no live login allowed). handlePay also has no try/catch, so the 404 becomes an unhandled promise rejection.

questions.question: Are there @Transactional annotations that look protective but are inert?
questions.why_it_matters: Multi-write paths without atomicity leave orphan rows or double-charge on retry.
questions.answer: Yes, 7. TransactionalOnlyOnPublicMethodsTest.KNOWN_INERT lists PlatformStatsAggregationJob#aggregateOne, PayoutService#doQueuePayout, WalletService#doProcessWithdrawal, MeeraSessionService#doSendTurn, MeeraSessionService#doPersistAssistantWriteback, CreateCampaignExecutor#doExecute and RequestPaymentExecutor#doExecute. Each is reached by a this.-invocation inside an idempotencyService.executeOnce lambda, and executeOnce is not transactional (IdempotencyService.java:131-165). WalletService is covered by an outer @Transactional on requestCreatorWithdrawal. MeeraSessionService.sendTurn and CreateCampaignExecutor.execute are NOT covered. ConfirmLaunchExecutor does this correctly through a `self` proxy (line 184), which shows the pattern was known and applied inconsistently.
questions.evidence: influora-api/src/test/java/com/influora/config/TransactionalOnlyOnPublicMethodsTest.java KNOWN_INERT list, which passes (2/2) and so still reflects reality; MeeraSessionService.java:326-352,354-357,548-575,606-607; CreateCampaignExecutor.java:138-170,207-208; ConfirmLaunchExecutor.java:177-184
questions.remaining_uncertainty: Whether a failure between the writes has occurred in production is unknown.

questions.question: Does the Meera confirm_launch path enforce the same campaign activation gates as the human publish path?
questions.why_it_matters: It decides whether a campaign goes ACTIVE, which charges the brand fee and invites creators.
questions.answer: No. CampaignService.update enforces validator.ensureEditable (rejects COMPLETED or CANCELLED), validateStatusForWorkspace (WORKSPACE_NOT_VERIFIED), validateHypeConfig, requireFundedEscrow and a locked load. ConfirmLaunchExecutor.doExecute only checks for a FUNDED hold and the ACTIVE-replay case, then calls campaign.setStatus(ACTIVE) (line 338) on an unlocked findByIdAndWorkspaceId. Campaign.setStatus is an unguarded setter. EscrowService.initiateFund has no verification gate either, so an unverified workspace can fund and then launch through Meera.
questions.evidence: CampaignService.java:243-380; CampaignValidator.java:62-122; ConfirmLaunchExecutor.java:220-340 (no Validator or VerificationStatus reference); Campaign.java:156-159; ConfirmLaunchExecutorTest only exercises DRAFT and ACTIVE sources
questions.remaining_uncertainty: Whether a CANCELLED campaign can still hold a FUNDED EscrowHold depends on the cancel/refund path, which I did not trace.

questions.question: Is the platform fee a single source of truth end-to-end?
questions.why_it_matters: Brands get quoted, and charged, from what the fee sources say.
questions.answer: No. There are at least 4 sources. (a) AmountDerivationService.deriveForCampaignIntent uses razorpayProperties.getPlatformFeePercent() = application.yml:407 ${PLATFORM_FEE_PERCENT:15.00}. This is the 'authoritative' Meera request_payment serverAmount. (b) BrandCampaignFeeService.resolveBrandFeeBps uses the PRO plan fee_bps, else platform_fee_config.brand_fee_bps (V42 seed 1000 = 10%), and is what is actually charged at publish. (c) BrandPlatformFeeService.getCurrentFee (/brand/platform-fee) returns brand_fee_bps only and ignores the PRO override, so PRO brands are shown 10% and charged the plan rate. (d) FE creator-chat.tsx:581 hardcodes PLATFORM_FEE_RATE = 0.15 even though api.wallet.platformFee (/creator/platform-fee) exists and admins can change the fee through PlatformFeeAdminService.update.
questions.evidence: AmountDerivationService.java:68; application.yml:407; BrandCampaignFeeService.java:108-122; BrandPlatformFeeService.java:47-58; V42__platform_fee_config_brand_fee_razorpay.sql:24,34; src/pages/creator-chat.tsx:579-585; src/lib/api.ts:3725-3729
questions.remaining_uncertainty: Live DB values for platform_fee_config and plans may have been changed by admins.

questions.question: Are duplicate-row races mapped to the intended error codes?
questions.why_it_matters: The FE branches on specific codes (creator-discovery.tsx:654 checks COLLABORATION_EXISTS).
questions.answer: Only in the non-race path. Collaboration and CreatorProfile use a caller-assigned String @Id with no @Version and no Persistable, so save() goes through merge() and defers the INSERT to flush/commit, outside the try block. In CreatorCampaignService.java:264, CreatorDiscoveryService.java:556, DealService.java:300 and CreatorProfileService.java:91,188, catch(DataIntegrityViolationException) can never fire. A concurrent duplicate surfaces through GlobalExceptionHandler:110 as a generic 409 DATA_INTEGRITY_VIOLATION instead of ALREADY_APPLIED, COLLABORATION_EXISTS or USERNAME_TAKEN. Other sites (AuthService:207, ExternalCreatorService:333, CreatorNudgeService:376) correctly use saveAndFlush.
questions.evidence: Collaboration.java:23-25; CreatorProfile.java:22-24; the listed catch sites; GlobalExceptionHandler.java:108-114; V6__creators_collaborations.sql:67 uq_campaign_creator
questions.remaining_uncertainty: Race-only. The sequential duplicate is caught earlier by collaborationReviveService.reviveOrRefuse.

questions.question: Is there mock or demo data reachable in a production build?
questions.why_it_matters: Fake data shown as real misleads users.
questions.answer: Mostly gated. StageLive, StageMatching, StageFunding and LivingCanvas branch on isApiLive(), and brand-chat's mock timeline is behind !isApiLive(). Two leaks remain. MeeraWorkspace.tsx:42 always themes /brand/meera with MOCK_BRAND_SNAPSHOT.brandColorHex (a fictional brand), and handlePay uses the demo campaign id in live mode. The admin OperationsSummary returns campaignsAtRisk hardcoded 0 (AdminDashboardService.java:119-121), which PulseDashboard.tsx:97 renders as a measured value. Mock fixture arrays (mockDealRooms and mockTimelineEvents in both chat pages, plus src/data/meera-mock.ts) ship in the prod bundle.

questions.question: Can the rate limiter be abused or leak memory?
questions.why_it_matters: It is the only abuse defence on the public webhook, tracking and festival endpoints.
questions.answer: AuthRateLimitFilter keeps Map<String, Window> windows = new ConcurrentHashMap<>() (line 283). The only write is windows.compute (line 306), and there is no remove, no scheduled cleanup and no size cap. Every distinct IP|bucket or user|bucket key lives for the life of the JVM, so unauthenticated GET /track/click from rotating IPs grows the heap without bound. The filter is also per-instance by design.
questions.remaining_uncertainty: The growth rate depends on traffic. It was not load-tested.

questions.question: Are money-safety gates actually switched on in the committed config?
questions.why_it_matters: Gates that default to off do not protect production.
questions.answer: The CR-51 escrow release gate (EscrowService.assertReleaseConditionSatisfied) is disabled unless INFLUORA_ESCROW_RELEASE_GATE_CUTOVER_INSTANT is set. No committed file under deploy/, docker/ or docker-compose.yml sets it (a grep finds only application.yml:155). A malformed value is logged and fails open (EscrowService.java:141-157). So in the committed configuration, escrow can be released for a collaboration with zero deliverables.
questions.evidence: application.yml:147-155; EscrowService.java:135-157,1545-1570; repo-wide grep for the env var name
questions.remaining_uncertainty: The value may be set in the server-side .env, which is outside the repo (CONFIGURATION provenance).

questions.question: Do swallowed exceptions hide failed business state?
questions.why_it_matters: Silent failures on money and compliance paths.
questions.answer: There are 234 broad catches (Exception, RuntimeException or Throwable) in src/main. Most are deliberate best-effort notifications. Two need attention. InvoiceService.applyD14GstBreakup (lines 248-267) swallows every failure and leaves a PAID subscription invoice with a null invoice_number and no GST breakup, with no durable marker (the Doc#2 path does have escrow_invoice_failures). EscrowService.applyFunding catches around notifyEscrowFunded, which calls the @Transactional (REQUIRED) CollaborationLifecycleService.onEscrowFunded inside the outer initiateFund/confirmFunded transaction. A runtime exception there marks the outer transaction rollback-only, so the catch cannot preserve 'funding already succeeded' as its log line claims.
questions.remaining_uncertainty: The onEscrowFunded throw path is low-probability (it mostly returns early). This is an inferred rollback-only interaction.

questions.question: Is there duplicated logic that must be kept in sync by hand?
questions.why_it_matters: Copies drift, and several already have.
questions.answer: Yes. (1) POST /wallet/escrow/fund is wrapped twice: api.ts:4090 payments.fundEscrow and meera-api.ts:661 fundEscrow (the comment at meera-api.ts:666 admits it). (2) mapShipmentApiStatusToUiStatus is duplicated in creator-chat.tsx:150 and brand-chat.tsx:615, and mayIndicateDealStatusChange in creator-chat.tsx:531 and brand-chat.tsx:589. (3) stringArg is copied in 6 Meera executors and decimalArg in 3. (4) The GST 18% rate appears as CommissionInvoiceService.GST_RATE (line 50) and as the literal 1.18 at InvoiceService.java:254. (5) The templateKey-to-eventType table in NotificationController.java:157-181 duplicates the notify() choices in NotificationListener. (6) sha256Hex/hmacHex exist in 5 private copies. (7) The AuthRateLimitFilter.bucketFor path strings duplicate the @RequestMapping paths.
questions.evidence: The file:line citations in the answer.

questions.question: Are API response and error conventions consistent?
questions.why_it_matters: FE parsing bugs of the 'lenient binding hides a shape mismatch' class.
questions.answer: No. 77 of 89 controllers return the ApiResponse envelope. Every Admin*Controller and PlatformFeeAdminController return bare DTOs, and a separate third FE client (src/admin/services/api-contracts.ts apiRequest) does not unwrap envelopes. AdminEmailController.sendBulk, AdminModerationController and AdminSupportController mix both conventions. Five admin calls bypass apiRequest with raw fetch and lose the 401 retry (api-contracts.ts:609,987,1164,1422 and auditLogger.ts:187).
questions.remaining_uncertainty: Each mixed-envelope admin endpoint's FE consumer was not traced individually.

questions.question: Are the unsubscribe links safe and correct?
questions.answer: GET /notifications/unsubscribe-link mutates state on a GET (NotificationController.java:192-219), so mail-scanner link prefetch (for example SafeLinks) can unsubscribe users without a click. The tokens have no expiry (UnsubscribeTokenService has no timestamp), yet the failure page says 'invalid or expired'. The business logic (a 23-entry mapping, entity upsert and inline-styled HTML) lives in the controller. HMAC comparison is constant-time (UnsubscribeTokenService.java:72), which is good.
questions.remaining_uncertainty: Prefetch behaviour depends on the recipient's mail provider.

questions.question: Does the frontend compile and are the audited backend suites green on the clean RC?
questions.why_it_matters: A baseline for every other claim.
questions.answer: Yes. `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` exits 0 with 0 'error TS' lines. `mvn -o test -Dtest=TransactionalOnlyOnPublicMethodsTest,ConfirmLaunchExecutorTest,CreateCampaignExecutorTest` passes: 2/9/13 tests run, 0 failures (surefire-reports). These are Mockito unit tests, so they cannot see the transactional or gate gaps above.
questions.remaining_uncertainty: The full mvn suite, vitest and eslint were not run by me (routed to Meera).

findings.title: Meera brand funding flow has no working live path: demo campaign id plus a link to a non-existent route
findings.evidence: MeeraWorkspace.tsx:21 `const MEERA_DEMO_CAMPAIGN_ID = 'meera_demo_campaign'` and :76-77 `api.payments.fundEscrow(MEERA_DEMO_CAMPAIGN_ID, idempotencyKey)`, wired to StageFunding's Pay CTA (StageFunding.tsx:120) in live mode too. EscrowController.fund -> EscrowService.deriveFundAmount findByIdAndWorkspaceId(...).orElseThrow returns 404. RequestPaymentExecutor.confirmActionUrl:181-183 returns '/brand/escrow/fund?campaignIntentId=...', which ToolResultRenderer.tsx:283-290 renders as a 'Confirm payment' link in a new tab, and App.tsx has no /brand/escrow route (falls to NotFoundPage at :883). handlePay has no try/catch. The idempotency key is `${id}-${Date.now()}`, a new key per click, so it provides no double-click protection.
findings.impact: The brand's Meera 'Fund & go live' either 404s silently (unhandled rejection) or opens a 404 page. Campaigns cannot be funded from the Meera surface, so confirm_launch always fails ESCROW_NOT_FUNDED unless the brand funds elsewhere.
findings.recommended_fix: Carry the real campaignId (from the create_campaign tool result or the CampaignIntent) into MeeraWorkspace. Replace handlePay with the existing useEscrowFund hook / FundEscrowButton (which already polls server state). Point confirmActionUrl at a real route (for example /brand/campaigns/:id?fund=1) or add the route. Generate the idempotency key once per intent, not per click. Add a vitest that asserts handlePay never sends MEERA_DEMO_CAMPAIGN_ID when isApiLive().
findings.verification_required: Meera/Neha: in staging, create a campaign via Meera, click Pay, and observe the POST /wallet/escrow/fund body and response; click 'Confirm payment' and observe the route.
findings.reproduction: Staging, live mode: /brand/meera -> reach funding stage after request_payment -> click Pay -> network shows campaignId=meera_demo_campaign -> 404 CAMPAIGN_NOT_FOUND.

findings.title: Self-invoked @Transactional on MeeraSessionService.doSendTurn and CreateCampaignExecutor.doExecute is inert, so their multi-write sequences are not atomic
findings.evidence: The repo's own TransactionalOnlyOnPublicMethodsTest.KNOWN_INERT lists 7 methods, and the test passed on the RC (2/2), which proves the list is current. MeeraSessionService.sendTurn (non-transactional, :326) -> idempotencyService.executeOnce (non-transactional, IdempotencyService.java:131-165) -> lambda `doSendTurn(...)` on this (:344). doSendTurn calls creditService.tryConsumeForTurn (a separate @Transactional bean, so it commits alone), then messageRepository.save, conversationRepository.save, a workspace lookup that can throw WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND, and token minting. A failure after the charge leaves the credit consumed and the reservation FAILED; a retry charges again. CreateCampaignExecutor.execute (:138, non-transactional) -> executeOnce -> this.doExecute (:170) writes campaignIntentRepository.save, campaignRepository.save, the intent again, toolCallRepository.save and the audit row (doExecute lines +77..+265). A failure after campaignRepository.save commits an orphan DRAFT campaign, and executeOnce marks the key FAILED, so the retry reclaims and creates a second campaign. ConfirmLaunchExecutor (:184) shows the correct `self.doExecute` proxy pattern. PayoutService and WalletService are documented or covered by an outer transaction. RequestPaymentExecutor.doExecute has only one real write (toolCallRepository.save), so it is lower risk.
findings.impact: A brand AI credit can be charged for a turn that was never persisted, and a retry double-charges. Meera create_campaign can leave orphan or duplicate DRAFT campaigns after a partial failure.
findings.recommended_fix: Use the proven ConfirmLaunchExecutor pattern: inject a @Lazy self and call self.doSendTurn / self.doExecute / self.doPersistAssistantWriteback, and make them public. Then delete those entries from KNOWN_INERT (the test forces this). Add an integration test (Testcontainers MySQL) that throws after campaignRepository.save and asserts zero campaigns.
findings.verification_required: Kabir/Meera: a mutation test that injects a failure after the first write, run against the real Spring context rather than Mockito.
findings.reproduction: Integration test: stub toolCallRepository.save to throw, call execute() through the Spring bean, then count campaigns (expect 0; the code path yields 1).

findings.title: ConfirmLaunchExecutor activates campaigns without the CampaignValidator gates the human publish path enforces
findings.evidence: CampaignService.update:243-380 runs loadOwnedForUpdate (a locked load), validator.ensureEditable (rejects COMPLETED/CANCELLED; CampaignValidator.java:72-79), validateStatusForWorkspace (WORKSPACE_NOT_VERIFIED; :62-70), validateHypeConfig, requireFundedEscrow and chargeOnPublish. ConfirmLaunchExecutor.doExecute:220-340 does an unlocked campaignRepository.findByIdAndWorkspaceId, checks only for a FUNDED hold and the ACTIVE replay case, then calls `campaign.setStatus(CampaignStatus.ACTIVE)` at :338. It contains no reference to CampaignValidator or VerificationStatus. Campaign.setStatus:156-159 is an unguarded setter. EscrowService.initiateFund has no verification gate. ConfirmLaunchExecutorTest covers only DRAFT and ACTIVE sources.
findings.impact: A workspace that is not VERIFIED can take a campaign ACTIVE (fee charged, creators invited) through Meera, which the PATCH path forbids. A PAUSED, COMPLETED or CANCELLED campaign that still has a FUNDED hold can be reactivated. HYPE campaigns can go live without a source reel. The unlocked load races against a concurrent PATCH.
findings.recommended_fix: Extract one CampaignActivationService.activate(campaign, workspace, source) that owns the locked load, the validator checks, requireFundedEscrow and chargeOnPublish. Call it from both CampaignService.update and ConfirmLaunchExecutor. Make Campaign.setStatus package-private or replace it with transitionTo(target) using an allow-list, as Collaboration.transitionTo already does.
findings.verification_required: Unit tests for confirm_launch with an unverified workspace, a CANCELLED campaign, and a HYPE campaign without a reel; each must return the same error codes as the PATCH path.
findings.reproduction: Workspace with verificationStatus != VERIFIED, DRAFT campaign with a FUNDED hold, confirm_launch through /internal/meera tool: the campaign becomes ACTIVE (the PATCH path would 403 WORKSPACE_NOT_VERIFIED).

findings.title: Platform fee resolved from 4 divergent sources (yml 15%, DB 10%, PRO plan override, FE hardcode 15%)
findings.evidence: AmountDerivationService.java:68 uses razorpayProperties.getPlatformFeePercent(), bound from application.yml:407 ${PLATFORM_FEE_PERCENT:15.00}, to compute the Meera request_payment serverAmount, which StageFunding renders as the authoritative 'Total to fund'. BrandCampaignFeeService.resolveBrandFeeBps:108-122 charges the PRO plan fee_bps, else platform_fee_config.brand_fee_bps (V42 seed 1000 = 10%). BrandPlatformFeeService.getCurrentFee:47-58 (/brand/platform-fee, used by brand-chat.tsx:696-705 and brand-campaign-detail.tsx:2068) returns brand_fee_bps only, with no plan check. creator-chat.tsx:581 has `const PLATFORM_FEE_RATE = 0.15;` although api.wallet.platformFee (/creator/platform-fee) exists and PlatformFeeAdminService.update lets admins change it. brand-chat.tsx:696 falls back to 15, not 10.
findings.impact: Meera quotes brands a total with a 15% fee while the actual publish fee is 10% (or the PRO rate). PRO brands see a 10% fee in campaign detail but are charged the PRO rate. Creators see a 15% deduction that goes stale the moment an admin changes the creator fee. These are trust and financial-display errors on money screens.
findings.recommended_fix: Make PlatformFeeService the single resolver: resolveBrandFeeBps(workspaceId) including the plan, and resolveCreatorFeeBps(). Have BrandPlatformFeeService and AmountDerivationService call it. Remove influora.razorpay.platform-fee-percent. In the FE, fetch the fee from api.wallet.platformFee in creator-chat, delete the constant, and never fall back to a guessed number (show '—' instead).
findings.verification_required: Test: a PRO workspace gets /brand/platform-fee feeBps equal to the plan fee_bps. Test: AmountDerivationService uses the same bps as chargeOnPublish.

findings.title: AuthRateLimitFilter window map never evicts entries (unbounded memory growth)
findings.evidence: `private final Map<String, Window> windows = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();` (:283). The only access is windows.compute(key, ...) at :306, which replaces expired windows but never removes keys. There is no @Scheduled cleanup, no size bound and no Caffeine or TTL cache. Keys are clientIp|bucket, or user:id|bucket for 13 user-keyed buckets. Unauthenticated buckets include GET /track/click, the public webhooks and the festival form.
findings.impact: Heap grows with every distinct client IP for the life of the JVM, and an attacker rotating IPv6 addresses can grow it quickly. The limiter is per-instance, so limits are also not global across replicas.
findings.recommended_fix: Replace the map with a bounded expiring cache (Caffeine expireAfterWrite = max bucket window, maximumSize) or Bucket4j. Longer term, enforce at the edge or with Redis.
findings.verification_required: A load test with N unique X-Forwarded-For/remote addresses, observing the map size or heap.
affected_features: Rate limiting (auth, OTP, tracking, webhooks, Meera turns, withdrawals)
findings.reproduction: Unit test: call doFilterInternal with 100k distinct remoteAddr values on /track/click and assert windows.size() stays bounded (it will be 100k).

findings.title: catch(DataIntegrityViolationException) around a deferred save() is dead code on 5 insert paths
findings.evidence: Collaboration (Collaboration.java:23-25) and CreatorProfile (CreatorProfile.java:22-24) have a caller-assigned String @Id with no @Version and no Persistable, so save() -> merge() defers the INSERT to flush/commit. Plain save() inside try/catch(DIVE): CreatorCampaignService.java:264, CreatorDiscoveryService.java:556, DealService.java:300, CreatorProfileService.java:91,188. The same codebase uses saveAndFlush correctly at AuthService:207, ExternalCreatorService:333 and CreatorNudgeService:376.
findings.impact: Under a concurrent duplicate, the client gets a 409 DATA_INTEGRITY_VIOLATION instead of COLLABORATION_EXISTS, ALREADY_APPLIED or USERNAME_TAKEN, so the FE-specific messages (creator-discovery.tsx:654) do not show. Side effects between the save and the commit (timeline/history writes) run before the rollback.
findings.recommended_fix: Use saveAndFlush inside these try blocks, matching the F-0785 fix already applied in CreatorNudgeService.
findings.verification_required: A Testcontainers MySQL test with two concurrent applies asserting the error code ALREADY_APPLIED.
findings.reproduction: Race two POSTs for the same (campaign, creator) pair.

findings.title: Escrow release gate (CR-51) is off by default and fails open on a bad value; no committed deploy config enables it
findings.evidence: application.yml:155 `cutover-instant: ${INFLUORA_ESCROW_RELEASE_GATE_CUTOVER_INSTANT:}` (empty default). EscrowService.initReleaseGateCutoverInstant:140-157 sets the value to null when it is blank or unparseable (a log.error, then fail-open). assertReleaseConditionSatisfied:1545-1551 returns early when not post-cutover. A grep of deploy/, docker/, docker-compose.yml and *.env* finds no setting.
findings.impact: Unless ops set the env var on the server, escrow can be released for a collaboration with zero deliverables. That is exactly the condition CR-51 exists to block.
findings.recommended_fix: Add the value to the prod env template and to SecretsStartupValidator (fail startup outside dev when it is blank). Treat an unparseable value as a startup failure, not fail-open.
findings.verification_required: Meera: check the live container env for INFLUORA_ESCROW_RELEASE_GATE_CUTOVER_INSTANT (read-only).
findings.reproduction: Read-only check of the server env.

findings.title: Subscription invoice GST breakup/number failure is swallowed with no durable marker
findings.evidence: InvoiceService.applyD14GstBreakup:248-267 wraps invoiceNumberService.generateNext, the GST split and the HSN lookup in catch(RuntimeException) -> log.error only. The invoice stays PAID with a null invoice_number and no GST breakup. By contrast, the Doc#2 campaign invoice path records escrow_invoice_failures with retry (CampaignServiceInvoiceService.java:336-515). The GST rate is also a bare literal `new BigDecimal("1.18")` at :254, duplicating CommissionInvoiceService.GST_RATE (:50).
findings.impact: Statutory invoices can silently lack a number or GST split, and the only record is a log line, which is a GST filing risk.
findings.recommended_fix: Reuse the escrow_invoice_failures-style durable marker and retry job for subscription invoices. Move GST_RATE into a single TaxRates constant or a config property.
findings.verification_required: A unit test forcing invoiceNumberService to throw, asserting a failure row is written.
findings.reproduction: Mock InvoiceNumberService.generateNext to throw during a subscription webhook.

findings.title: Unsubscribe is a state-mutating GET with non-expiring tokens and business logic in the controller
findings.evidence: NotificationController.unsubscribeViaLink (@GetMapping, :192-219) upserts EmailPreference directly through the repository. It uses a 23-entry TEMPLATE_KEY_TO_EVENT_TYPE map (:157-181) that must mirror NotificationListener's notify() templateKeys, and inline-HTML rendering (:221-236). UnsubscribeTokenService has no timestamp or expiry. NotificationController also calls notificationRepository directly 10 times.
findings.impact: Link-prefetching scanners can unsubscribe users. Leaked tokens are valid forever. The mapping drifts when a new template is added (the fallback silently no-ops, the F-0444 class of bug).
findings.recommended_fix: Serve a GET confirmation page and POST the unsubscribe (with a List-Unsubscribe-Post one-click header per RFC 8058). Move the mapping into the email template registry next to each template, so the key and eventType are defined once. Move the persistence into NotificationPreferenceService.
findings.verification_required: none beyond a code change and unit test
findings.reproduction: GET the link with a HEAD/GET-prefetching client.

Java: DealService 2523, CreatorNudgeService 2357, EscrowService 1900, ContractService 1539, PortfolioService 1352, CreatorDeliverableService 1253, SubscriptionService 1198, CreatorDiscoveryService 1127, AuthService 945, AdminBrandService 938, AdminCustomEmailService 874, NotificationListener 872, ExternalCreatorService 829, MeeraSessionService 772, WalletService 753. CreatorNudgeService also embeds a text-safety engine (normalizeForMatching 150 lines, Devanagari confusable folding, isWordFlank, firstUnsafeTopic) while a separate 43-line TrendHeadlineScreener exists; 10 of its 11 commits landed in the last 9 days as 'repair rounds'.

Chat pages -> shared useDealRoom hook plus DealTimeline, ProposalCard and ShipmentPanel components used by both the brand and creator pages.

findings.title: Inconsistent API envelope and three FE API layers
findings.evidence: 77 of 89 controllers use ApiResponse<>. No Admin*Controller does, except partial use in AdminEmailController.sendBulk (:116-117), AdminModerationController and AdminSupportController. PlatformFeeAdminController returns bare DTOs (:62-94). FE: src/lib/api.ts (7037 lines, unwraps the envelope), src/lib/meera-api.ts (905), and src/admin/services/api-contracts.ts (1546, apiRequest returns the raw body at :157-163, no unwrap). Five raw fetch() calls bypass apiRequest's 401 retry (api-contracts.ts:609,987,1164,1422; auditLogger.ts:187).
findings.impact: Every new endpoint risks a shape mismatch that lenient TS casting hides. api.ts at 7037 lines is a merge-conflict hotspot, and a concurrent session edits this repo.
findings.recommended_fix: Pick one envelope for all controllers (a ResponseBodyAdvice can wrap bare returns). Generate FE clients from OpenAPI (springdoc) into per-domain modules, and delete the hand-written duplicates.

findings.title: Mock fixtures and scratch artifacts ship in the prod bundle and the repo
findings.evidence: mockDealRooms and mockTimelineEvents are defined in both creator-chat.tsx (:235,:324) and brand-chat.tsx (:269,:353). src/data/meera-mock.ts is imported by 6 production components. .proof-os has 1676 tracked files (22 MB), including 25 .ts/.tsx/.java copies such as .proof-os/tasks/T-F0324/brand-wallet.wrongfix.tsx. scratch_jwks_repro/ and screenshots/ are tracked. graphify-out/graph.json, which the audit brief says exists, is absent in the RC.
findings.impact: Bundle weight. The risk of a demo branch rendering in live mode (see KAV-01/KAV-10). Tooling noise, which vitest.config.ts:19-37 already has to work around.
findings.recommended_fix: Move demo fixtures behind a dynamic import() gated on !isApiLive() or into a separate demo entry. Move .proof-os task artifacts out of git or into LFS.
findings.verification_required: Meera: vite build --report to confirm the fixtures are in the prod chunk.

findings.title: Swallow-after-inner-@Transactional in EscrowService.applyFunding cannot protect the outer commit
findings.evidence: EscrowService.applyFunding (private, called from the @Transactional initiateFund and confirmFunded) wraps notifyEscrowFunded in catch(RuntimeException) with the log line 'funding itself already succeeded' (:510-519). notifyEscrowFunded calls CollaborationLifecycleService.onEscrowFunded, a public @Transactional REQUIRED method on another bean (:147-152), which joins the outer transaction. A RuntimeException that crosses that proxy marks the transaction rollback-only, so the outer commit throws UnexpectedRollbackException and the funding is rolled back.
findings.impact: Low probability (advance() mostly returns early), but the code's stated guarantee is false. A webhook-confirmed payment would 500 and be retried.
findings.recommended_fix: Publish a domain event handled @TransactionalEventListener(AFTER_COMMIT), or mark onEscrowFunded REQUIRES_NEW / noRollbackFor, as the code intends.
findings.verification_required: Integration test: make collaborationRepository.save throw inside onEscrowFunded and assert the hold ends FUNDED.
